audit.whatIsWrong: Hexplosive Minefield is named four times purely as a zoning wall — 'wall the chokes', 'a Q he can flatten with Hexplosive Minefield', 'bait the minefield onto the wave' — and the property that decides how to cross it is never stated.
audit.why: Successive mine detonations on the SAME target deal reduced damage. For a melee champion with three dashes that inverts the instruction completely: walking the long way around a minefield costs tempo she does not have, while dashing straight through it costs one full mine and then progressively less. The field is 16 seconds flat at every rank, so it is also the only Ziggs cooldown that does not shorten as the game goes on. 'Bait the minefield onto the wave, then walk the gap it leaves' is slower and worse than simply going through.
audit.corrected: Hexplosive Minefield (E), 16s flat, 900 range: repeat detonations on the same target deal reduced damage. Dash through the field, don't path around it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ziggs.json — E Hexplosive Minefield: 'Successive mine detonations on the same target deal reduced damage', cd 16

audit.whatIsWrong: Satchel Charge is the tracked, matchup-defining ability across every string in the full layer — 'engage when it's down', 'track it before every engage', 'commit on Satchel Charge's cooldown' — and its cooldown is never given. Bouncing Bomb's range and cooldown are likewise missing.
audit.why: Satchel Charge is 20 seconds at rank 1. That single number is what makes the entry's whole plan real: it is simultaneously his knockback and his only escape, so the twenty seconds after he spends it are a window in which a champion with no mobility is standing in front of three dashes and a 1250-range blink. Bouncing Bomb at 850 range against Cunning Sweep's 650, returning every 6 seconds, is likewise the concrete version of 'out-ranges your whole kit'.
audit.corrected: Satchel Charge (W), 20/18/16/14/12: knockback and his only escape. Bouncing Bomb (Q), 6/5.5/5/4.5/4 at 850 range against your 650. Commit inside the Satchel's 20s.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ziggs.json — W cd 20/18/16/14/12, Q cd 6/5.5/5/4.5/4 range 850

audit.whatIsWrong: Two strings credit Ambessa with 'R's flat armor-pen passive and on-hit healing' / 'R's armor-pen passive and on-hit heal' (spikes[3].text, whys[5]). Short Fuse is never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Public Execution grants no armour penetration and no healing in Riot's text — blink to the farthest champion in a chosen line, suppress, slam for damage and a stun. The kit file's 'heal' flag on her R is a tooltip-parsing misfire (see notes), and against a squishy artillery mage the invented shred is not even needed: first-item physical damage on a champion with no mobility is the whole argument. Short Fuse is the genuine gap — his next attack periodically deals bonus magic damage and that cooldown shortens every time he casts an ability, so his poke rhythm is cast-then-step-up-and-hit, and the step-up is the tell Ambessa is waiting for.
audit.corrected: Short Fuse (P): a periodic bonus-magic-damage attack whose cooldown drops every time he casts. His cast is the tell that a step-up attack is coming.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ziggs.json — P Short Fuse: 'Periodically, Ziggs' next basic attack deals bonus magic damage. This cooldown is reduced whenever Ziggs uses an ability.'

audit.whatIsWrong: The difficulty labelling contradicts itself three ways. diff reads 'FAV' while diffRating reads '8.5/10' and breakdown.difficulty renders that same number as 'Overall difficulty: 8.5/10'; tone is #ff5d6c, the red used by HARD matchups elsewhere in this file; and report[14] prints 'Hard matchup — difficulty 8.5/10'. Meanwhile tldr opens 'He kites you out — survive' while content.mid says 'This is where you take over' and content.late says 'You still win the straight fight'.
audit.why: 53.41% over 264 games is a favourable lane and the prose agrees, so 'FAV' is probably the correct badge and 8.5/10 is probably a favourability score being re-rendered as a difficulty score by breakdown.difficulty and report[14]. I did not touch diff, diffRating or tone — they are mirrored against a Ziggs page that has not been audited, and the fix here is a rendering decision rather than a content one. I did rewrite tldr, which is prose and mine to fix, so the summary line no longer contradicts the two paragraphs underneath it.
audit.corrected: Rewrote tldr to match the FAV badge and the body text. The diffRating/breakdown.difficulty/report[14] labelling conflict needs a human — see questionsForUser.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[] and phases[].side give Ziggs five of seven stages, while the phase RATINGS on those same cards read 7/10 and 8/10 — favourable to Ambessa — and the prose gives her everything from level 3 onward ('the lane flips at 3', 'this is where you take over', 'he is dead').
audit.why: Side, rating and text disagree on the same card, and the rating agrees with the prose and with the win rate against the side. That is the same inversion pattern several other entries in this file carry, and here the internal rating field is effectively a second witness against the side value. I did not flip it — chart edits apply atomically and mirror against the Ziggs page — but this one has the strongest evidence of the five I found.
audit.corrected: Sides should follow the ratings and the prose: Ziggs at 1-2, Ambessa from 3 on. Needs a human decision — see questionsForUser.

audit.why: The wave plan is right and, unusually, it is right for a stated reason: hold the wave near your side so a champion with no mobility has to walk up to farm. Against Ziggs specifically that is the mechanism that spends Satchel Charge, because stepping up into Lacerate range is when he needs the escape. I only added the 20-second figure that turns it into a countable trade.
